question: What does WACC stand for?
before: Weighted Average Cost of Capital. Blends cost of all capital sources (debt and equity) by proportion.
after:
Concept: WACC stands for Weighted Average Cost of Capital. It represents the average rate a company must pay to finance its assets, blending the cost of equity and cost of debt weighted by their respective proportions in the capital structure.

Why this is correct: Option B uses the exact terminology standard across corporate finance and equity research. WACC is the benchmark discount rate used in DCF valuation and capital budgeting decisions. Every analyst uses this term consistently when evaluating a company's cost of raising capital.

Why the others are wrong: Option A (Weighted Adjusted Cost of Capital) inserts "Adjusted" — an incorrect modifier that is not part of the standard definition. Option C (Weighted Average Cost of Credit) confuses the concept by substituting "Credit" for "Capital," missing that WACC includes both debt (credit) and equity funding sources. Option D (Weighted Annual Cost of Capital) mistakenly adds "Annual" — WACC is not specifically annualized in its naming convention; the rate itself is expressed as an annual percentage, but the acronym does not use that word.

Intuition: Getting the terminology right is foundational. WACC is the single most important discount rate in equity research — every DCF model, every investment decision, and every capital allocation debate hinges on accurately calculating and interpreting it. Precision in naming reflects precision in concept.
